articles.title: US intel says Putin ordered NATO sabotage drive, Leipzig drone attack an opening shot
articles.desc: The report raises the perceived risk of escalation between Russia and NATO, which would tend to support European defence stocks and weigh on European risk sentiment if officials respond with tougher measures. The energy channel is the one to watch: Russia’s diesel supply deal with Washington and the
articles.content: The report raises the perceived risk of escalation between Russia and NATO, which would tend to support European defence stocks and weigh on European risk sentiment if officials respond with tougher measures. The energy channel is the one to watch: Russia’s diesel supply deal with Washington and the pause in new US sanctions were aimed partly at keeping Moscow out of the war with Iran, so any rupture in that arrangement could tighten fuel markets already strained by the Middle East conflict. Drone strikes on commercial ships in the Black Sea add a shipping risk premium near NATO waters. For now, the report adds detail and attribution rather than a new event, so the market impact may be limited unless governments act on it. - The Leipzig attack was already pinned on Russian military intelligence, but the WSJ’s reporting moves the responsibility up to Putin himself and shows how close Germany came to invoking NATO’s mutual defence clause. Summary: US intelligence agencies say Putin directly ordered an intensified campaign of sabotage and covert action against NATO countries, according to European officials cited by the Wall Street Journal (gated) The failed August drone attack on a cargo plane at Germany’s Leipzig-Halle Airport was one of the campaign’s opening shots, they said Aides to Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Germany would have considered invoking NATO’s Article 5 had the attack caused heavy casualties Western intelligence traced the operation to a unit of Russia’s military intelligence, with logistics run through Serbia, where seven suspects have since been arrested A Kremlin back-channel contact warned Berlin after the attack that it would not be the last Russia denies involvement in sabotage in Europe US intelligence agencies have concluded that Russian President Vladimir Putin personally ordered a stepped-up campaign of sabotage and covert action against NATO countries, with a failed drone attack on a German airport in August among its first operations, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing European officials briefed on the findings. The attack at Leipzig-Halle Airport, one of Europe’s largest air-cargo hubs, targeted an Antonov freighter used to carry military aid to Ukraine. Germany formally blamed Russia for the attempt in September. The Journal’s reporting goes further, placing the order at the top of the Kremlin and framing Leipzig as part of a deliberate escalation. Aides to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the newspaper that had the attack caused large numbers of casualties, Berlin would have considered invoking Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, the collective-defence clause that obliges allies to come to a member’s aid. It has been invoked only once, after the September 11 attacks in 2001. According to investigators cited by the Journal, at least three drones loaded with Semtex were hidden near the airport perimeter and controlled remotely through German mobile networks. One struck the freighter without exploding. German cyber officials traced the communications to servers previously used by Russia’s military intelligence agency. Western officials attributed the campaign to a GRU branch known as the Special Tasks Service, formed in 2023, and traced the Leipzig plot to one of its department chiefs, already under EU and UK sanctions. Investigators believe a former Russian officer coordinated the ground logistics with Belarusian operatives, using Serbia as a hub to move drones and explosives. Serbian prosecutors have since arrested seven suspects. The report said European officials have seen a sharp rise in so-called grey-zone attacks since August, including arson against drone makers in Estonia and Poland, sabotage of Starlink stations in Poland, Lithuania and Bulgaria, and drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea. After the Leipzig attempt, a Kremlin back-channel contact reportedly warned Berlin that more attacks would follow. Russia has denied involvement, with Putin questioning in September where the evidence was. The Kremlin did not respond to the Journal’s request for comment. The findings come as Washington pursues a delicate relationship with Moscow, including a diesel supply arrangement and a pause in new sanctions that President Donald Trump has said is aimed at keeping Russia out of the war with Iran. How European governments respond, and whether Washington adjusts its approach, will be the next test. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.desc: Market Analysis by covering: Nasdaq 100, US Dollar Index Futures, Brent Oil Futures, United States 10-Year. Read 's Market Analysis on Investing.com
articles.content: US Dollar Weakness Breaks From Oil as US Tech Takes Control of FX Direction | Investing.com US Dollar Weakness Breaks From Oil as US Tech Takes Control of FX Direction US Dollar Weakness Breaks From Oil as US Tech Takes Control of FX Direction US Dollar Weakness Breaks From Oil as US Tech Takes Control of FX Direction Brent’s attempts to break above $110 a barrel are not preventing the greenback from falling. The US dollar is reacting more to corporate earnings than to geopolitics. The US dollar is retreating for the fourth day running, despite ’s attempts to hold onto the key $110-per-barrel level. The last time Brent crude was seen at these levels was in May, when significant disruptions to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz prompted the conclusion of a fragile and short-lived peace agreement between Washington and Tehran. This time, according to estimates by the US Department of Energy, export volumes from the Middle East stand at 80% of pre-war levels. Nevertheless, a substantial geopolitical risk premium is preventing oil prices from falling. According to Kpler, 18 ships have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz over the past two weeks. Coupled with the Houthis’ ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia, this is keeping tensions high in the Middle East. With its back against the wall, Iran has no choice but to assert its control over the world’s key oil artery. The fall in Brent prices is being held back by an increase in tanker traffic bound for China and a significant reduction in global stocks. At the start of the conflict in the Middle East, these stocks served as a buffer, holding back the rally in North Sea crude. The IEA has now announced the release of the final 100 million barrels from strategic reserves, forming part of the 400-million-barrel batch agreed in March. Beijing’s growing appetite for oil is giving the bulls confidence. The divergence between Brent and the US dollar is driven by a shift in market narratives. In the recent past, the greenback strengthened against the backdrop of an oil rally, serving as both the currency of an energy-exporting nation and a safe-haven asset. Currently, the is showing greater sensitivity to developments in the US equity market. ’s worst weekly performance since April 2025 triggered a plunge in amid strong demand for safe-haven assets. The US dollar has lost its main trump card, especially as the likelihood of the Fed tightening monetary policy in October has diminished. However, once technology shares recovered, the fall in the USD index slowed. As a result, the forex market is paying more attention to corporate earnings reports than to news from the Middle East. articles.title: India Freezes Trading Accounts Worth ₹2 Billion in Stock-Tip Probe
articles.desc: The Directorate of Enforcement searched 29 premises as it investigated WhatsApp promotions involving shares of two listed companies.
articles.content: India Freezes Trading Accounts Worth ₹2 Billion in Stock-Tip Probe | EconoTimes India’s Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has frozen trading accounts worth about ₹200 crore (2 billion rupees) as it investigates alleged WhatsApp stock promotions tied to subsequent share sales. The investigation concerns R M Drip and Sprinklers Systems Ltd. and R&B Denims Ltd. The ED said the number of buyers rose for both stocks during the promotion campaign. It separately reported increases in R M Drip’s share price and trading volume while that stock was being promoted. People who had received shares through preferential allotments then sold some of their holdings to investors, the agency alleged. The two companies issued more than 35 million shares and convertible warrants to selected people and entities between April 2023 and March 2024, according to the ED. The agency traced a substantial share of the allotment payments to connected individuals, firms and lenders. From late December 2025 through February 2026, investors received daily recommendations to buy the shares in WhatsApp groups, including one named “Multibagger Stocks,” the ED said. The groups operated from Bhavnagar, Gujarat, and used SIM cards obtained in other people’s names in Haryana and Mumbai, according to the agency. Investigators searched 29 premises in Mumbai, Nashik, Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat and Bhavnagar on Oct. 16 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The ED said it seized digital devices, share-transaction records, property documents and other papers. It said the frozen accounts belonged to people and connected entities under investigation. Zerodha co-founder and CEO Nithin Kamath warned in an Oct. 20 post on X that similar schemes may become more frequent as the market cycle advances. He pointed to promotions of stocks and initial public offerings through messaging groups and influencers. “This is probably the silliest way to lose money,” Kamath wrote. The ED did not give a figure for investor losses. Its investigation is continuing. articles.content: Wärtsilä wins repeat six-engine order for two Brazilian iron ore pusher tugs ПАО "ДВМП" ИНН 2540047110 ERID: 2W5zFHrvuLC ООО "Газпромнефть Марин Бункер" ИНН 7838392447 ERID: 2W5zFGkoFyS Wärtsilä wins repeat six-engine order for two Brazilian iron ore pusher tugs Wärtsilä wins repeat six-engine order for two Brazilian iron ore pusher tugs Wärtsilä has won a repeat order to supply six engines for two inland waterway pusher tugs being built in Brazil for LHG Mining, according to a company statement. Brazilian shipyard Estaleiro Rio Maguari is building the vessels, with each tug to be powered by three Wärtsilä 20 engines. The order was booked in the third quarter of 2026. The tugs will transport iron ore from the Corumbá region as part of LHG Mining’s river logistics operations on the Paraguay-Paraná waterway, one of South America’s main inland transport corridors. “As we continue to expand our inland logistics fleet, reliability, efficiency and operational consistency remain important considerations,” LHG Mining president Darlan Carvalho said. “The Wärtsilä 20 engine platform has proven well suited to our application, and this follow-on order allows us to build upon an established concept while supporting the long-term development of our transport operations.” Wärtsilä’s scope also includes tools and spare parts, a specific fuel oil consumption guarantee, commissioning support and an extended warranty. “This contract represents another important milestone in our collaboration with both LHG Mining and Wärtsilä,” Estaleiro Rio Maguari commercial director Fabio Vasconcellos said. “The project builds on experience already gained through the earlier vessels and helps ensure efficient execution as we continue delivering modern river transport assets for the Brazilian market.” The Wärtsilä 20 engine can operate on a range of fuels, including biodiesel blends. “Inland waterways play a vital role in moving essential cargo efficiently and reliably across South America. As operators continue to invest in growing and modernising their fleets, they need partners that can support both their operational needs today and the long-term performance of their assets throughout the vessel lifecycle,” Wärtsilä Marine general manager for Latin America sales Mário Barbosa said. “This repeat order reflects the confidence placed in Wärtsilä’s technology, local expertise and long-term support capabilities, and we look forward to continuing our collaboration with LHG Mining and Estaleiro Rio Maguari on this important project,” he added. The equipment is scheduled for delivery during 2027. The order follows a 2025 contract covering the same engines for four similar vessels. Wärtsilä also has service agreements covering other vessels in LHG Mining’s fleet. Wärtsilä Corporation develops engines, propulsion systems, hybrid technology, exhaust treatment, shaft-line equipment and digital and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. Estaleiro Rio Maguari is a Brazilian shipyard. LHG Mining operates the inland logistics fleet covered by the project. Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) DIXFIELD — The Select Board voted 5-0 on Oct. 12 to purchase a 2027 Freightliner plow truck for $224,164 for Public Works, a truck they learned they could not lease. Town Manager Alicia Conn explained that on Feb. 23, the board voted to lease a Freightliner for five years for snowplowing from Freightliner of Maine in Bangor. The town has the truck, which replaces a 2016 Freightliner plow truck the town had spent $40,000 on repairs over the past couple of years. “In trying to put together the paperwork, our financials are not gathered to the point that we can bring them together for a lending situation right now,” Conn said. “We really don’t have a choice. We can buy the truck outright because we have $369,255 in reserve currently, or we can hold off on paying on the truck we’ve already received.” Conn noted that the town is still going through its 2023 audit, and accounting for 2024 and 2025 is still ongoing. “That paperwork is not in order and because of that, we can’t go through lending,” she said. At the June town meeting, $125,000 was put into the Public Works reserve fund, so “we do have the funds available in our reserve account at this point,” Conn added. “We didn’t back in February when we voted on it initially.” She said the entire fleet for public works is now complete and paid for. The new Freightliner joins a modernized lineup consisting of a 2025 Western Star, a 2026 Freightliner, and a 2025 one-ton truck. The long-term goal established by Conn is to maintain a predictable, timely replacement schedule for municipal vehicles to prevent severe winter service disruptions caused by equipment failures. Conn added that at an upcoming Select Board meeting, it will be decided about putting the 2016 Freightliner up for auction, something the town has had better results from than soliciting bids. articles.title: Starbucks Stock Rises Near $100 as Investors Bet on Brian Niccol's Turnaround Ahead of Key Earnings Report
articles.desc: Starbucks shares rose nearly 2% towards $100 as investors anticipated the company's fourth-quarter results and assessed progress under CEO Brian Niccol's turnaround strategy.
articles.content: Starbucks Stock Rises Near $100 as Investors Bet on Brian Niccol's Turnaround Ahead of Key Earnings Report NEW YORK — Shares of Starbucks rose nearly 2% on Tuesday, climbing toward the $100 mark as investors continued to bet on the coffee chain's recovery under CEO Brian Niccol ahead of its next quarterly earnings report. Starbucks shares gained $1.88, or 1.92%, to $99.75 in morning trading on the Nasdaq. It was not immediately clear whether Tuesday's gain was tied to specific news. The move comes as investors prepare for the company's fiscal fourth-quarter results, which Starbucks typically reports in late October. Starbucks has staged a notable recovery since Niccol, the former Chipotle chief executive, took over in September 2024. At the time, the company was struggling with falling sales, long wait times and customer complaints about its stores and pricing. Niccol launched a "Back to Starbucks" strategy aimed at improving service, simplifying the menu and operations, reducing discounting and restoring the coffeehouse atmosphere that once defined the brand. The company reintroduced seating, revamped its ordering system and added new menu items to draw customers back. Last month, Niccol declared the two-year turnaround effectively complete. "Starbucks is back," Niccol said in an interview on CNBC's "Squawk Box." In a letter to employees, he said the company had returned to growth, delivered positive global same-store sales and improved its margins. Niccol said the company's next priority is renovating thousands of its cafes. Starbucks' most recent quarterly results showed the turnaround gaining momentum. In its fiscal third quarter, which ended June 28, Starbucks reported a 7.9% increase in global comparable store sales, its fourth straight quarter of same-store sales growth. The gain was driven by a 4.2% increase in transactions and a 3.5% rise in the average ticket, a sign that more customers were returning to stores. Adjusted earnings came in at 85 cents per share on revenue of $9.3 billion, both well above Wall Street expectations. "This was the quarter our momentum became truly measurable," Niccol said when the results were released. The company raised its outlook for fiscal 2026, projecting adjusted earnings of $2.55 to $2.65 per share, up from earlier forecasts. It also projected that global same-store sales would rise nearly 6% for the year, with U.S. same-store sales up more than 6%. A key measure of Starbucks' recovery has been customer traffic. Earlier this year, the company reported transaction growth for the first time in two years, including among both members and non-members of its loyalty program. Analysts say rising traffic is especially important because it shows customers are returning, rather than simply paying higher prices. Starbucks has also focused on speeding up service. The company rolled out scheduled ordering and other changes designed to reduce wait times, particularly during busy morning hours. Outside the United States, Starbucks has shifted toward a more asset-light business model. Following the formation of a joint venture in China, roughly 90% of the company's international locations are now licensed rather than company-operated, according to Niccol. Investors often favor licensing arrangements because they can provide steadier profits with lower capital costs. International same-store sales rose 5.7% in the most recent quarter. In August, Starbucks said it would cut more than 200 corporate jobs, including about 120 employees on a coffeehouse design and development team who declined to relocate from Seattle to Nashville, Tennessee. articles.desc: ECG announces a nationwide meter audit to cut commercial losses and curb electricity theft. Customers can verify field staff by dialling *226# or 0302 611 611.
articles.content: ECG announces nationwide meter audit to curb power theft | 3News The Electricity Company of Ghana Limited (ECG) has announced that it will soon begin a Nationwide Meter Audit Exercise across all its operational areas, as part of efforts to reduce commercial losses, improve revenue assurance, and combat electricity theft. In a public announcement, the company said the exercise will involve inspecting and verifying all prepaid and postpaid meters, Special Load Tariff (SLT) installations, and associated wiring. The aim is to confirm the integrity of metering systems and ensure accurate measurement and billing of electricity consumption. ECG said the announcement serves as official notice of the exercise and that no further prior notices, appointment letters, or advance notifications will be issued. It therefore advised customers, landlords, estate managers, property managers, facility managers, and security personnel that the absence of a separate notification letter shall not be a basis for denying, restricting, or delaying access to authorised ECG personnel. The company also reminded the public of Regulation 4(h) of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (Customer Service) Regulations, 2020 (L.I. 2413). The regulation requires a consumer to grant a utility’s employee or agent safe and reasonable access to the consumer’s premises to read a meter or check utility equipment. This is subject to the production of a verifiable identity card, and to the agent following the access procedure prescribed in the utility’s Customer Charter. ECG said all its employees and authorised agents taking part in the exercise will carry official ECG identification cards. Customers are encouraged to verify the identity of field personnel before granting them access, through either of two channels: the Customer Call Centre line, 0302 611 611; or the *226# USSD verification code, available on all mobile networks. Enter the 6-digit verification code provided by the staff member. Check that the staff member’s full name, region, and district are displayed. Confirm that the information matches the staff member assisting them. For further information, customers can contact the ECG call centre on 0302 611 611 or reach the company on social media via @ECGghOfficial on Facebook, X, Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. articles.desc: For this week's segment, Re Pierce sent in this question: "Wanted to ask how to get rid of those robocalls, those spam calls that we're getting on iPhones."
articles.content: How to block unwanted calls and texts | Nydia Knows - 6abc Philadelphia How to block unwanted calls and texts | Nydia Knows How to block unwanted calls and texts | Nydia Knows For this week's "Nydia Knows" segment, Re Pierce asked, "Wanted to ask how to get rid of those robocalls, those spam calls that we're getting on iPhones." So Re, here is your answer! There is a call-blocking feature you can activate on both iPhone and Android! On your iPhone, go to Settings - Apps - Phone. Then scroll down to Call Filtering. Turn on Call Filtering for SPAM. Then calls identified as spam or fraud by your carrier will be silenced, sent to voicemail, and moved to the Spam list. One caveat: your carrier does have to support this feature. On iPhones, you can also "Silence Unknown Callers" so calls from unsaved numbers will go straight to your voicemail. You can always pick up as they're leaving a voicemail if it turns out to be someone you do want to talk to.. Or you can call them back later. On Android, open your Phone app. Then tap the three dots or menu icon. Then go to Settings - Caller ID and Spam - and turn on "Filter Spam Calls." articles.desc: Search engines are losing their share of traffic to news publishers as artificial intelligence reshapes how users discover information online,
articles.content: AI search cuts publisher traffic as search engines lose ground – Businessday NG Log in or create a free account to get started. AI search cuts publisher traffic as search engines lose ground Search engines are losing their share of traffic to news publishers as artificial intelligence reshapes how users discover information online, Search engines are losing their share of traffic to news publishers as artificial intelligence reshapes how users discover information online, with new data from audience analytics firm, Chartbeat pointing to a growing challenge for digital media organisations. Chartbeat’s third-quarter 2026 audience report found that search engines accounted for just 12 percent of pageviews among publishers in North America, down from 21 percent a year earlier. In Africa, however, search accounted for 46 percent of publisher pageviews, up from 41 percent over the same period which highlights regional differences in how audiences access online content. The findings come as search platforms integrate generative artificial intelligence into their results, providing users with summaries and direct answers that can reduce the need to visit the websites that originally published the information. For publishers that depend on search traffic to attract readers, the shift raises concerns about audience reach, advertising revenue and the sustainability of online journalism. Chartbeat’s data indicates that the decline is not limited to North America. Search traffic has also lost ground across several European regions, suggesting that changes in digital discovery are affecting publishers across multiple markets. In Northern Europe, search engines accounted for 13 percent of publisher pageviews in the third quarter, compared with 19 percent a year earlier. Southern Europe recorded a decline from 33 percent to 25 percent, while Central and Eastern Europe fell from 27 percent to 19 percent. The figures measure search engines’ share of total pageviews rather than absolute traffic volumes. Consequently, a declining share does not necessarily mean that visits from search engines fell by the same percentage, as changes in traffic from other sources can also affect the proportion. AI-generated answers challenge traditional search traffic The shift reflects a broader change in how people use search engines. Traditional search typically directs users to a list of websites, leaving them to select sources and navigate individual pages for answers. AI-powered search experiences synthesise information from multiple sources into a single response. Although these systems may cite or link to publishers, users can obtain the information they need without clicking through to the original articles. Data previously published by Chartbeat showed that pageviews from Google Search across its publisher network fell 34 percent between December 2024 and December 2025, while traffic from Google Discover declined 16 percent over the same period. The analytics firm also reported that referrals from ChatGPT grew by more than 200 percent year-on-year. However, AI chatbots still accounted for less than 1 percent of total pageviews across its network, indicating that the growth in AI referrals had not yet compensated for declining search traffic. The figures suggest that while AI tools are becoming more important in online discovery, they remain a relatively small source of overall publisher traffic. The changing search landscape has also affected publishers differently according to their size. Chartbeat data reported by Axios showed that small publishers lost 60 percent of referrals from search over two years, compared with 47 percent for medium-sized publishers and 22 percent for larger organisations. Smaller publishers may have fewer resources to invest in audience development, subscription products, newsletters and other distribution channels that reduce dependence on search engines. articles.title: DHS Orders DeepSeek Wiped From Civilian Federal Computers Over China Spy Fears
articles.desc: DHS has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek AI products, citing risks that sensitive U.S. data could be transferred to China.
articles.content: DHS Bans DeepSeek From Federal Civilian Agency Systems DHS Orders DeepSeek Wiped From Civilian Federal Computers Over China Spy Fears Federal civilian executive-branch agencies have been told to rip DeepSeek out of their computer systems entirely, with the Department of Homeland Security warning that the Chinese AI company's products could funnel sensitive U.S. government data straight to Beijing. The order bans not just DeepSeek's own apps, but any future purchases of its technology by those agencies; it excludes Department of Defense and intelligence-community procurements, as well as national security systems. It reaches further than most people might expect, sweeping in third-party software quietly built on top of DeepSeek's models. , DHS ordered federal civilian executive-branch agencies to immediately remove AI products and services developed by DeepSeek from their IT systems and prohibit any future procurements. The same outlet reports the order covers products built by Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., its affiliates, and any third-party offerings constructed using DeepSeek's underlying technology — a detail that could make compliance messy, since it is not always obvious which software was built on DeepSeek's back end in the first place. flagging a practical headache: it is not clear which third-party products and services have been developed using DeepSeek's wares, the outlet notes, meaning agencies may struggle to even identify everything they're supposed to pull. Treasury, State and Justice Among Agencies Covered Per CNBC, the directive applies to federal civilian agencies including the Treasury, State and Justice departments, as part of what the outlet describes as a Trump administration effort banning DeepSeek-related technology from federal civilian IT systems over cited security concerns. The Defense Department and the intelligence community are carved out of the ban, since the order applies specifically to civilian executive-branch procurements. The exclusion is also spelled out by meritalk.com, which reports the order applies to federal civilian executive branch agencies but excludes procurements by the Department of Defense and the intelligence community, as well as national security systems. Those exempted arms of government already have their own, separate restrictions in place. DHS Cites Malware Risk and Data Flowing to China The justification laid out by Homeland Security goes beyond generic caution. Per , DHS warned that the models themselves may contain malware or other security vulnerabilities — language that treats DeepSeek's software less like a foreign competitor and more like a potential Trojan horse sitting on government networks. , DHS said DeepSeek presents multiple threat vectors and that its use may result in the transfer of sensitive data to China. CyberScoop, in its own review of the order, reported that DHS said the data could produce actionable intelligence on U.S. persons and/or government programs — a framing that casts the risk not as abstract cybersecurity hygiene but as a potential window into the lives of American citizens and the inner workings of federal programs. DHS also grounded its order in existing law, with CyberScoop noting the notice cites the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Act and a review by the Federal Acquisition Security Council — the kind of bureaucratic machinery that federal agencies typically invoke only when they intend a restriction to stick. Confusion Over When the Order Was Actually Signed Exactly when this all started remains murky. CyberScoop reported on a letter from Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin ordering the exclusion of DeepSeek products on June 26, while Econotimes reported that the order, signed by Mullin, lists July 24, 2026, as its original release date. Whichever date is accurate, meritalk.com reports that DHS made the order public on October 19 through a Federal Register notice scheduled for publication the following

articles.content: Former Comcast exec tapped to head biz services at Mediacom Former Comcast exec tapped to head biz services at Mediacom Mediacom has appointed Wolfgang Lewis as SVP and GM of business services. He most recently led Comcast Business's national enterprise field sales organization. #pressrelease Mediacom Communications today announced the appointment of Wolfgang Lewis as Senior Vice President and General Manager of Business Services. In this role, Lewis will lead the strategy, sales, and operations of Mediacom's commercial business, driving profitable revenue growth across Small and Medium Business (SMB), Enterprise, Wholesale, Carrier Services, and National Accounts. Reporting to Toni Murphy, Executive Vice President of Operations, Lewis will be responsible for further unlocking the multi-billion-dollar addressable marketing opportunity that is Mediacom Business, from go-to-market strategy and sales execution to order management, customer onboarding, and customer success. His focus will be on strengthening the customer experience, expanding market opportunities, and delivering sustainable growth. Lewis is an accomplished commercial growth executive with extensive experience leading sales and operating organizations serving small business, mid-market, state and local government and education (SLED), and enterprise customers. He most recently led Comcast Business's national enterprise field sales organization, overseeing more than 1,000 sales professionals responsible for supporting over $2 billion in annual revenue. His responsibilities included go-to-market strategy, sales execution, forecasting, budgeting, product launches, and sales methodologies. During his career at Comcast, Lewis held a series of leadership positions with increasing responsibility. Before leading Enterprise Field Sales, he served as Vice President of Field Sales for Comcast Business's West Division, overseeing commercial sales organizations across the western United States. He previously served as Regional Vice President for Comcast Business in the Midwest and held leadership positions in the company's Beltway and Mountain West regions. articles.title: Once globally preeminent, US universities are sliding into decline
articles.content: Once globally preeminent, US universities are sliding into decline – KIRO 7 News Seattle Once globally preeminent, US universities are sliding into decline The nation was distracted by other things when a quiet warning sounded: Support was diminishing for American academic research that had led to breakthroughs and innovation. That familiar-sounding worry came not this year, but near the end of World War II, in by the wartime Office of Scientific Research and Development. The response then: infusions of government cash that would propel the U.S. higher education system into international preeminence over the subsequent decades. American colleges and universities rose to the ranks of the best in the world. They attracted top scholars who won a disproportionate number of . They helped drive the innovation economy. As trade deficits beset other industries, education became . At their peak enrollment, international students brought in Now, as a new academic year begins, American dominance in higher education globally is incontrovertibly in decline, according to data, international rankings and independent experts, according to The slide has been accelerated by a year and a half of funding cuts, restrictions on international students and curbs on what can be said or taught. But it began before those political challenges, with , lackluster returns on ever-rising prices and public mistrust. “It takes a while for all of these problems to trickle down, but they are beginning to trickle down,” said Eric Mlyn, a faculty fellow at the Kenan Institute for Ethics at Duke University who studies academic freedom. Top scholars are leaving. Fewer international students are coming. U.S. universities are slipping in international rankings. And American universities have failed to keep pace as other countries pour resources into their higher education systems. Chinese institutions, for example, have increased their production of graduates with doctoral degrees much faster than American ones in the critical fields of science, technology, engineering and math. Rather than expanding, U.S. doctoral programs are now admitting fewer candidates or have stopped accepting new applicants altogether. This has myriad impacts on all Americans. Falling behind in research imperils the nation's economic competitiveness, for instance. And attracting fewer international learners — and the subsidies they represent to universities' bottom lines — is already affecting the services and majors available to domestic students, and could increase the cost. So dire has the situation become that the American Academy of Arts and Sciences hosted a discussion about it in June. The title: “Is the U.S. Losing Its Edge as a Global Education Leader?” The answer is yes, said Mlyn, who was one of the panelists. “There are so many issues threatening America’s global standing,” he said. of the QS World University Rankings has fallen from 31 to 26 in the past 10 years, while Chinese universities are moving up. The Times Higher Education World University Rankings still puts seven U.S. universities among the top 10. But the smallest number ever International standings like these “are the global symbol for geopolitical strength on the world stage, and they’re very influential in people’s decision about where to study,” said Phil Baty, the Times Higher’s chief global affairs officer. “If you start seeing the slow diminution of rankings, that means you’re becoming less attractive to that talent. Then it could be a really serious downward spiral.” In the next Times Higher rankings — due out Sept. 30 — U.S. institutions continue to fall in comparative measures of reputation and research quality, Baty said. “It does feel like a tipping point,” he said. in science, technology, engineering and math than U.S. universities do, according to the National Science Foundation, or NSF.
